key_insight: Parallel-SFT trains supervised fine-tuning tasks in parallel across multiple programming languages during RL training so that coding skills learned in high-resource languages transfer zero-shot to low-resource languages, improving cross-language generalization for code RL models like Llama-3.1.
problem_solved: Reduces the failure of RL-trained code models to generalize from high-resource programming languages to lower-resource ones without requiring per-language RL data or retraining.
method: Run supervised fine-tuning tasks for multiple source languages in parallel (Parallel-SFT) to preserve language-agnostic coding skills during RL optimization.
Combine the parallel SFT stage with RL updates performed on a high-resource language so the model learns reward-driven behaviors while retaining cross-PL generalization.
Balance data and shared parameters (or lightweight language-specific modules) to encourage transfer rather than overfitting to any single programming language.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy RL-enhanced code models across many programming languages with far less target-language data and tuning, accelerating multilingual coding assistance and reducing maintenance cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: multi-language supervised fine-tuning branches running in parallel → centralized RL updates → single multilingual model for zero-shot inference.
Before/after bar chart or heatmap comparing zero-shot performance on low-resource PLs with and without Parallel-SFT.
Schematic illustrating shared parameters vs. language-specific modules to explain where transfer happens.
Example code prompt in a high-resource PL and corresponding zero-shot output in a low-resource PL to show qualitative transfer.
paper_title: Parallel-SFT: Improving Zero-Shot Cross-Programming-Language Transfer for Code RL
paper_authors: Zhaofeng Wu, Shiqi Wang, Boya Peng, Anuj Goyal, Melanie Kambadur
